description.summary: web views hosted by a media centre compositor

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a compositor that hosts a web browser as one of its clients drive the browser's views and learn their state, so that the compositor can present a page as part of its own user interface: open a URL on the user's behalf, navigate, show the title and favicon, offer bookmarks, and hand input to the page while it is in front.
The compositor spawns the browser itself and the browser connects over an inherited socket. The browser is the Wayland client: requests are what the browser tells the compositor, events are what the compositor asks of the browser.
Views are grouped by profile. A profile names a hermetic set of cookies, storage and credentials kept by the browser; views of different profiles never share them. The compositor decides which profile a URL opens in and what that profile looks like to the web: user agent, user scripts and content filters are configured per view before the first page loads, as file descriptors the browser reads.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes are done by bumping the version number in the protocol and interface names and resetting the interface version.

interface.name: kodi_web_manager_v1

description.summary: create and announce web views

interface.description:
The global through which the browser announces itself and creates views. A browser binds it once.
The compositor asks for a view of a profile with the want_view event; the browser answers with a create_view request for that profile. The browser may also create views on its own, for example the warm default view it keeps ready at start-up. One view per profile: a second create_view for a profile the compositor already knows is a protocol error.

entry.name: duplicate_profile
entry.summary: a view for this profile already exists

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface already has a role or belongs to another view

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager

request.description: Destroy the manager. Existing views are unaffected.

request.name: create_view

description.summary: create a view for a profile

request.description:
Create a view that renders into the given surface. The surface becomes the view's output and must not have another role; the browser gives it its toplevel role through xdg_wm_base as usual, the compositor configures it fullscreen at its own resolution.
The profile names the hermetic storage this view uses. The compositor configures the view with set_user_agent, add_user_script and add_content_filter events before its first load_url, so the browser must not load anything into a fresh view on its own.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface the view renders into

request.name: ready

description.summary: the browser is ready to serve views

request.description: Sent once the browser's engine processes are up and it can create and load views without further start-up cost. The compositor shows no web entry point as available before it.

event.name: want_view

description.summary: the compositor wants a view for a profile

event.description:
The compositor needs a view for the given profile and none exists. The browser answers with create_view for that profile. If it cannot, it answers with a view_unavailable request.
The uplink names the local source address every connection of the profile's view is bound to, so that a host with more than one uplink can choose the one a profile leaves through. It is an IPv4 address, an IPv4 subnet such as 192.168.5.0/24, or an interface name; a subnet or an interface name is resolved for every new connection, so it survives a new DHCP lease. A connection whose uplink does not resolve fails rather than leaving through another uplink. An empty string leaves the connections to the system's routing. A browser that cannot bind connections answers a non-empty uplink with view_unavailable.

arg.name: uplink
arg.summary: source address, subnet or interface, or empty

request.name: view_unavailable

description.summary: a wanted view cannot be created

request.description: The browser cannot create the view asked for by want_view, for example because the profile's storage is unusable.

interface.name: kodi_web_view_v1

description.summary: one web view of one profile

interface.description:
A view is one page container bound to one surface. The compositor drives it with events and learns its state through requests.
Configuration events (set_user_agent, add_user_script, add_content_filter) apply to this view only and take effect from the next navigation. They arrive before the first load_url of a view the compositor asked for.
An inactive view keeps its page alive: media keeps playing and scripts keep running, so that the user can leave the page and come back to it. The browser may lower an inactive view's rendering frequency. The compositor stops a view's media by loading about:blank, and discards a view with the close event.

enum.name: error_code

description.summary: what went wrong with a view

enum.description: Reported by the error request. The message carries the engine's own text for the log; the code is what the compositor acts on.

entry.name: load_failed
entry.summary: the page could not be loaded

entry.name: tls_failed
entry.summary: the TLS handshake or certificate check failed

entry.name: engine_crashed
entry.summary: the engine process rendering this view terminated

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the view

request.description: The browser is done with the view. Sent in answer to the close event, or on its own when the view can no longer be served, after an error request. The surface loses its role.

request.name: url_changed

description.summary: the view's URL changed

request.description: Sent whenever the committed URL of the view changes, including fragment navigation within the page.

request.name: title_changed

description.summary: the page title changed

request.description: Sent whenever the document title changes. An empty string means the page has no title.

request.name: favicon

description.summary: the page favicon is available

request.description: Hands the compositor the page's favicon as an ARGB8888 wl_shm buffer. The compositor copies what it needs and releases the buffer with wl_buffer.release; the browser destroys it after the release. A view sends a new favicon request whenever the icon changes.

request.name: load_progress

description.summary: load progress of the current page

request.description: Progress of the current load in percent, 0 at the start of a navigation and 100 when the load finished.

request.name: navigation_state

description.summary: history availability changed

request.description: Whether the view can go back or forward in its history.

request.name: error

description.summary: the view failed

request.description: Something went wrong with the view. After engine_crashed the browser either recovers the view, in which case it follows up with url_changed, or destroys it.

event.name: set_user_agent

description.summary: set the user agent of this view

event.description: The user agent string this view presents. Takes effect from the next navigation. A view configured without it uses the browser's default.

event.name: add_user_script

description.summary: inject a user script into this view

event.description: A script the browser injects into every document of this view at document start, in the main world, before any page script runs. The script is read from the file descriptor, which the browser closes; the compositor keeps no interest in it afterwards. Scripts apply in the order they are added.

event.name: add_content_filter

description.summary: apply a content filter to this view

event.description: A request filter the browser applies to every load of this view, in the content blocker JSON format WebKit and Safari share. The browser compiles it once per name and keeps the compiled form across runs; a filter sent again under the same name replaces the earlier one.

event.name: load_url

description.summary: load a URL

event.description: Navigate the view to the URL. about:blank unloads the page and stops its media.

event.name: navigate

description.summary: history and load control

event.description: Go back or forward, reload, or stop the current load.

event.name: set_active

description.summary: the view is shown or hidden

event.description: Active means the compositor presents the view's surface and routes input to it. An inactive view keeps running and may render less often; it must still commit a frame when its content changes, so that the compositor has a current picture when it activates the view again.

event.name: close

description.summary: the compositor is done with the view

event.description: The browser unloads the page, unmaps the surface and destroys the view. The profile's storage stays.
